title: 2026 Science Nobel Prizes Go to Brain Light Switches, Ghost Particles and Mirror Molecules
summary:
Every year, Nobel Prizes are given for some of the most important work in science. The 2026 prizes honored work in biology, physics and chemistry.

The physics prize went to the man behind the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole. It helped find tiny, ghostly particles called neutrinos coming from outside our solar system. The chemistry prize honored work on molecules that are mirror images of each other, like your left and right hands.

The medicine prize went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. They found a way to turn brain cells on and off with light.

It started with a tiny green alga. Hegemann and Nagel found a protein in it that makes an electric signal when light hits it. Deisseroth's team put this protein into nerve cells. When light shined on them, the cells switched on. In mice, blue light even moved their whiskers.

Scientists hope this tool can help treat problems like blindness.
why_it_matters: These discoveries started with curious questions about tiny things, just like the questions kids ask every day.
